summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests ubamatamab with and without marlotamig (REGN7075) in adults with advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer. Both drugs are given as described in the protocol, and sarilumab is also given to help with immune-related side effects of ubamatamab; how often and for how long treatment lasts is not stated. The record does not state a primary outcome measure, but it says the study looks at how well the drugs work, their side effects, their levels in the blood, and antibodies against them.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa ubamatamab con y sin marlotamig (REGN7075) en adultos con cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas avanzado o metastásico. Ambos fármacos se administran según lo descrito en el protocolo, y también se administra sarilumab para ayudar con los efectos secundarios relacionados con el sistema inmunitario causados por ubamatamab; la frecuencia y la duración del tratamiento no se indican. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal, pero señala que el estudio analiza qué tan bien actúan los fármacos, sus efectos secundarios, sus niveles en la sangre y los anticuerpos contra ellos.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with advanced or metastatic NSCLC (stage IIIB not suitable for chemoradiotherapy, stage IIIC, or stage IV).
Received appropriate first-line standard treatment for advanced or metastatic NSCLC, as described in the protocol.
Has tumor tissue available for MUC16 testing by immunohistochemistry.
Has at least one radiographically measurable lesion by CT or MRI per RECIST v1.1.
not_for: Disease progressed fewer than 84 days after starting first anti-PD-(L)1 therapy.
Toxicity from prior treatment not resolved to grade 1 before starting study treatment (with listed exceptions).
Untreated or active primary brain tumor, CNS metastases, leptomeningeal disease, or spinal cord compression.
Investigational drug given within 4 weeks before the first study dose, or current participation in another investigational study.
Anti-EGFR antibody therapy within the drug-specific window before the first study dose.
